title: Self-Generated In-Context Examples Improve LLM Agents for Sequential Decision-Making Tasks
claim: Growing a per-step retrieved bank with the agent's own successes: ALFWorld unseen 73 -> 89% (gpt-4o-mini, 5 seeds); baseline is a fixed 18-example human bank, not no memory; high seed variance; no random-bank control. [verification: T]

title: AdaMEM: Test-Time Adaptive Memory for Language Agents
claim: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, ALFWorld seen: no memory 45.2, AdaMEM-low 54.0 (main table); ablation AdaMEM-max 65.5, without strategy 59.3, strategy without memory 34.8; temperature 0.7; bank of 1,596 own train successes; top-1 retrieval. [verification: T+K]

title: TRAD: Step-Wise Thought Retrieval and Aligned Decision
claim: GPT-4, ALFWorld unseen: random same-type examples 89.8 = task retrieval (Synapse) 89.6 < step retrieval by thought with a window 96.8. 'Random' draws within the task type (checked in code). [verification: T+K]

title: ExpeL: LLM Agents Are Experiential Learners
claim: gpt-3.5, ALFWorld, Table 3 (example selection ablation): ReAct 40.0, random successful 42.5, reasoning similarity 48.5, task similarity 59.0; unclear whether the random row keeps insights. [verification: T]

title: Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents: Learning to Learn from Experience
claim: 3-8B models, scripted-expert bank: retrieval once ~ every step for whole trajectories (64.2 vs 63.8, k=4); the no-memory arm lacks admissible actions, so much of the gain is format; a mismatched-type bank gives little on hard tasks; learning from failures only after retrieval-aware fine-tuning. [verification: T]

title: When Successful Memories Mislead Embodied Agents (MATE)
claim: Old ALFWorld action syntax in the bank drops Qwen2.5-14B from 72.4 to 20.1 (single run); normalising 19 of 877 lines restores 82.1; with a bank from the same executor, raw trajectories are best (79.9). [verification: T]

title: More Memory, Worse Agents: Error Reproduction and Anti-Persistence
claim: Abstraction or joint memory worse than trajectory memory in 7 of 9 settings; discarding synthesised guidance after use beats storing it (Llama ALFWorld 54.7 vs 26.7); ScienceWorld held-out: trajectory memory helps (Llama-4-Scout 9.4 -> 20.0). [verification: T; ScienceWorld numbers spot-checked]

title: EffectMem (EMNLP 2026 Findings)
claim: Applicability-gated contracts with fallback to the plain policy; Qwen3-8B ALFWorld 38.3 -> 91.8, ScienceWorld 15 -> 65 (single seed, multi-agent pipeline); the gate alone takes ScienceWorld 15 -> 51. [verification: T (spot-checked)]

title: SWE-ContextBench
claim: Retrieved summaries without an oracle fall below no memory (22.2 vs 26.3); oracle 34.3; top-1 retrieval hits the related task 18% of the time. [verification: T (spot-checked)]

title: ReasoningBank
claim: WebArena +4 to +7 points; k=1 best (49.7), falling to 44.4 at k=4; learns on the test stream with an LLM judge (72.7% accurate). [verification: T (spot-checked k sweep)]

title: SWE-Exp
claim: SWE-bench Verified: one retrieved experience is best (42.0) versus two (39.8) and four (39.0). [verification: T (spot-checked k sweep)]

title: Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory
claim: ALFWorld test, GPT-4o: no memory 42.14, trajectories 74.29, trajectories+scripts 77.86; retrieval once by task; random vs retrieved only on TravelPlanner (74.59 vs 73.38). [verification: T (spot-checked)]

title: Synapse: Trajectory-as-Exemplar Prompting with Memory
claim: Mind2Web GPT-3.5: retrieved exemplars add only +1.4/+1.5/+0.2 step SR over fixed exemplars; most of the gain comes from format and state abstraction. [verification: T (helper, not spot-checked)]

title: RAP: Retrieval-Augmented Planning with Contextual Memory
claim: The one paper retrieving windows of steps during the episode (ALFWorld GPT-3.5 52.2 -> 85.8 with 3 trials); the plain variant learns from the test stream. [verification: T (helper)]

title: Imagine-then-Plan
claim: One harness, single run: RAP adds +9.3 for Qwen3-8B (19.29 -> 28.57) and +1.43 for Llama-3.1-8B (21.43 -> 22.86) on ALFWorld; it lowers Qwen3-8B's two-object tasks 25.0 -> 4.2. [verification: T (spot-checked)]

title: SeqMem-Eval
claim: Qwen3-8B ALFWorld: no memory 52.9, G-Memory 62.9, ExpeL single-attempt 59.3, multi-attempt 79.3 (confounded by attempts); online gains vanish on hold-out for API tasks. [verification: T (spot-checked)]

title: Remember Me, Refine Me (ReMe)
claim: Qwen3-8B: BFCL-V3 40.33 -> 45.17, AppWorld 14.97 -> 24.70 (Avg@4); A-Mem and LangMem below no memory on AppWorld; a usage-scenario key beats the raw task description. [verification: T (spot-checked)]

title: HiPlan
claim: The agent moves the tomato into the microwave without cooling it for 'put a cool tomato in the microwave' (adjective-form goal failure). [verification: T (spot-checked quote)]

title: Towards Autonomous Agents: Adaptive-planning, Reasoning, and Acting in Language Models
claim: gemma-2-9b-it fetches the desklamp first for 'examine the cd with the desklamp' and substitutes a handtowel for a cloth. [verification: T (spot-checked quote)]

title: Coarse-to-Fine Grounded Memory (CFGM)
claim: ALFWorld GPT-4-turbo 80.6 -> 91.0; key = task description; k=2-3 best, k=5 falls back to 81.3 (helper). [verification: T (helper)]

title: Spinning Straw into Gold (HSL)
claim: Failed runs relabeled as successes for goals they reached (90% relabel accuracy), used for fine-tuning a 1B model, not in context. [verification: T (helper)]

title: CTIM-Rover
claim: Negative result: no memory arm beat the baseline on 45 SWE-bench tasks (42% vs 40%); one misleading rule hurt. [verification: T (helper)]

title: Reflexion published ALFWorld logs (our analysis)
claim: A single retry at temperature 0 solves 10 of 50 failed tasks (17 over six retries); 161/200 reflections copy the prompt example; 22 reflections (18 distinct) state a false precondition (open the microwave/fridge); the PDDL does not require it and 22/22 replayed walkthroughs that never opened the appliance were won. [verification: P (our count)]

title: Qwen3-4B no-memory episodes in the AdaMEM harness (our analysis)
claim: 12/20 and 14/20 solved (bf16, FP8, temperature 0.7), 4/20 flip; adjective-form goals 3/3 fail in both; desklamp 2/2 fail; sequential search uses the step limit. Hypotheses from 20 tasks. [verification: P (our count)]

title: CPU checks of ALFWorld data and public banks (our analysis)
claim: Adjective-form goals are 28% of valid_seen and 25% of valid_unseen; walkthrough replay 30/30 admissible; 90-92% of trajectories in ETO, AgentTraj-L and AgentBank have an action not matching the current templates; ETO median 8 steps vs walkthrough 6; the harness orders games by an unsorted os.walk. [verification: P (our count)]

title: Useful Memories Become Faulty When Continuously Updated by LLMs
claim: Repeated LLM consolidation degrades memory across seven frameworks; episodes carry the gain, abstractions alone fall to the no-memory level. [verification: T]

title: AutoManual
claim: ALFWorld unseen 97.4% (GPT-4-turbo) with rules built online; offline rules weaker (90.7). [verification: T (helper)]

title: When Continual Learning Moves to Memory: A Study of Experience Reuse in LLM Agents
claim: Raw trajectories transfer negatively across different tasks; abstract procedural insights transfer more reliably (two runs per condition). [verification: T]

title: Retrieval-Augmented Reinforcement Learning (R2A)
claim: Querying with the agent's raw state gave no gain; an information bottleneck and a separate query mattered. [verification: T (helper, partial)]

title: Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations: What Makes In-Context Learning Work?
claim: Classification-style ICL: randomly replacing labels in demonstrations barely hurts across 12 models; the label space, input distribution and format drive the effect. [verification: A]

title: How Should Agents Read Demonstrations? Hierarchical Structure Beats Flat Action Logs
claim: Identical action sequences, different organisation: named subgoal groups raise the pass rate 76.7 -> 90.7% on 43 vaguely described web tasks (win-loss 6:0); flat logs give a smaller, non-significant gain; no format helps on 42 precise tasks. [verification: T (abstract and setup)]
